title: Bunny Bell and the Wobbly Seven
markdown:
In a town of tinkling bells and giggling gardens lived Bunny Bell, quite possibly the fluffiest bunny you ever did see, ears that danced when she was excited, which was often, especially about shiny things. Her burrow overflowed with pebbles like tiny stars, dewdrops in acorn cups, and a lost button that gleamed like a pearl. Her heart went thump-thump-thump at every new glint.

Every day she woke to sunbeams on her nose, hopped out, and polished her collection on mossy shelves, humming tunes like bubbling brooks and dreaming of the next sparkle. The button went in the middle. The dewdrops had to sit where they would not spill. The star-pebbles she lined up by how loudly they winked. She was ever so good at finding things. She was also a little impatient. If a shine sat just out of reach, her whiskers drooped, then she grabbed with a frantic wiggle.

Look twice, Bell. The shine can wait.

Until one day the Grand Town Clock let out a particularly loud BONG, and something slipped. Down tumbled a perfect golden Seven, plink into the sparkling fountain in the square. Big, bright, brassy, winking like a playful eye.

Bunny Bell, mid-clover, ears flopped. “The clock coughed up a number. And it’s gone into the fountain.” So shiny. So solid. Bobbing just out of reach. She stretched. She hopped onto a mossy stone at the rim. Whoosh — back feet slid, fluffy poof onto grass. She tried again from the other side, paws dripping, clover forgotten. The Seven bobbed just out of reach, as if it were teasing. A very shiny, very bobbing problem.

She needed help. Cog the brass squirrel lived in the oak by the library, clever as he was shiny, gears whirring when he thought. She scampered, fluff bouncing. “Cog. The clock dropped a Seven. It’s too watery.”

Cog’s brass ear twitched. He scurried down the oak, tick-tock feet on rough bark, and peered with glass-marble eyes. He reached. Clink — fingers only brushed the cool surface. He tapped his chin, soft clicks. Trickier than a lost acorn.

His mind whirred through an old library book, pages thin as butterfly wings, the one he kept under a knothole so the rain could not make the ink run. When light travels from air into water it slows, and things look bent or shifted — like a straw in a glass gone wiggly. He had tested it once with a twig in a rain-cup. The twig had lied. “Aha. Bell, I have an idea. A bit wobbly.”

He explained in metallic chirps. “Because the Seven is underwater, it looks a little different than it is. Water plays a trick, bending light. If we look at where it seems to sit, then aim just below, we might grab the real Seven hiding under the illusion.”

Bunny Bell’s ears perked. A funhouse mirror in the fountain. Silly and smart.

Look twice, Bell. The shine can wait.

They tried once the impatient way, because Bunny Bell’s paws itched. Cog lowered the grabber toward the wink they could see. The wire kissed empty water. The Seven bobbed, still there, still lying. Bunny Bell’s ears drooped. Cog’s gears clicked a patient little rhythm, the same one he used when a lost acorn was not where it pretended to be.

Cog stood on the mossy edge, gleaming. Bunny Bell’s paws twitched. He squinted through ripple. “It looks a little higher than it is. So we aim just a bit lower.” He lowered a long thin grabber of bent wire and a tiny spring, to the spot a hair below the watery Seven. Plink, plink, the wire whispered. Bunny Bell held her breath so hard her ears went still. A soft thud. A gentle scoop. Up it came, dripping, smelling of moss and sun: the shining Seven, a newly discovered jewel.

Bunny Bell’s ears did a happy wiggle. She took it with trembling delight. “Thank you. Cleverest brass squirrel.”

Cog bowed, precise. “It’s all about looking a little differently.”

They carried the Seven across the square, past the clover she had dropped and the stone that had whooshed her. Fountain water dotted the cobbles. Cog climbed the clock face with tick-tock care, found the empty place where a number ought to sit, and pressed. The Seven clicked home. The next chime sounded like a friend who had been swimming.

Ever since then she still collected shiny things with all her heart — and she took a breath and looked twice before she grabbed. Look twice, Bell. The shine can wait. She and Cog, the wobbly-water team, kept an eye on the clock in case it coughed again.
characters: Bunny Bell (a bunny), Cog (a brass squirrel)
author: StoryGen Community
